nodes.name: PhantomBuster Webhook
nodes.notes: responseMode=onReceived acks PhantomBuster immediately (its webhook timeout is 11s) so downstream processing never risks a timeout retry/duplicate delivery.

nodes.name: Fetch Agent Info
nodes.notes: Returns the agent's orgS3Folder and s3Folder, used to build the URL to its full accumulated output file (every lead this agent has ever scraped, not just this run's new finds). This is what lets us catch up on companies that were scraped in a past run but never made it into the Prospects sheet — PhantomBuster's per-run resultObject/container data only covers what changed THIS run, and with Watcher Mode on, a company already scraped produces nothing new even if our pipeline failed to process it last time.

parameters.url: ={{ (() => { const arg = JSON.parse($('Fetch Agent Info').first().json.argument || '{}'); const csvName = arg.csvName || 'result'; const a = $('Fetch Agent Info').first().json; return `https://phantombuster.s3.amazonaws.com/${a.orgS3Folder}/${a.s3Folder}/${csvName}.json`; })() }}

nodes.name: Fetch Result (Try JSON)
nodes.notes: No PhantomBuster auth needed — direct S3 object URL. Reads the configured output filename from the agent's own settings (argument.csvName from Fetch Agent Info) instead of assuming 'result'. Tries the .json extension first; onError is set to continueErrorOutput so a 403/404 (agent's Results File format is actually CSV) falls through to 'Fetch Result (CSV Fallback)' automatically instead of failing the whole run — no manual guessing of the format needed.

parameters.url: ={{ (() => { const arg = JSON.parse($('Fetch Agent Info').first().json.argument || '{}'); const csvName = arg.csvName || 'result'; const a = $('Fetch Agent Info').first().json; return `https://phantombuster.s3.amazonaws.com/${a.orgS3Folder}/${a.s3Folder}/${csvName}.csv`; })() }}

nodes.name: Fetch Result (CSV Fallback)
nodes.notes: Only runs when the JSON attempt errored. Same csvName, .csv extension, fetched as raw text so the next Code node can parse it — PhantomBuster's own S3 output is either JSON or CSV depending on this agent's Behavior > Results File setting, and this path covers CSV without you needing to check which one it is.

nodes.name: Normalize JSON Result
nodes.notes: Success path from 'Fetch Result (Try JSON)'. Unwraps whatever shape PhantomBuster's JSON export uses (bare array, or {candidates:[...]}/{data:[...]}/{rows:[...]}/{results:[...]}) into a single {candidates: [...]} item so both the JSON and CSV paths converge on the same shape. Confirmed via a real run that this agent's JSON export wraps the array under a top-level 'candidates' key — the earlier version of this node didn't check for that key and silently produced an empty array even when the S3 file had real data.

nodes.name: Parse CSV Result
nodes.notes: Error/fallback path from 'Fetch Result (CSV Fallback)'. Hand-rolled CSV parse (handles quoted fields and embedded commas) since PhantomBuster's CSV export has no fixed column set to hardcode against — turns it into the same {candidates: [...]} shape 'Normalize JSON Result' produces.

nodes.name: Candidates Ready
nodes.notes: Junction point both the JSON and CSV paths converge on — whichever one actually ran, downstream nodes reference this single node name ($('Candidates Ready')) instead of needing to know which format the fetch used.

nodes.name: Read All Companies
nodes.notes: Reads every row (no Status filter here — the filtering happens in the next Code node) so we can compare against the full accumulated candidate list and find companies still not Done.

nodes.name: Filter To Pending Companies
nodes.notes: This is the fix for "Success / Input already processed" leaving companies permanently stuck: instead of only looking at this run's new finds, it cross-references the FULL accumulated candidate list against which companies are still not marked Done in the Companies sheet, and processes those — regardless of which run originally scraped them. Check this node's output first if results are empty: confirm the S3 result file actually parsed ('Candidates Ready') and that your Companies sheet's 'Company Name' values exactly match candidate.companyName from PhantomBuster (case differences are already normalized, but typos/extra spaces in the sheet won't match).

nodes.name: Pace (light safety margin)
nodes.notes: OpenAI's paid-tier rate limits are far more generous than Groq's free tier (new accounts start around 500 RPM / 200,000 TPM for gpt-4o-mini, scaling up with usage history) — a 1s delay is just a light courtesy pace, not a hard requirement like the old Groq pacing was.

nodes.name: OpenAI - Qualify Candidate
nodes.notes:
Set the 'Header Auth' credential on this node after import: Name = Authorization, Value = Bearer YOUR_OPENAI_KEY (include the word 'Bearer' and a space before the key). gpt-4o-mini: $0.15/$0.60 per 1M tokens (input/output) — at ~450-500 tokens/call this is roughly $0.0001-0.0002 per candidate. Requires a funded OpenAI Platform (api.openai.com) account with billing set up — a ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription does NOT include API access or credits, they're billed completely separately.

Field names match the Account Employees Export phantom's confirmed output schema: fullName, title, titleDescription, companyName, companyUrl, location, companyLocation, duration, profileUrl, profileImageUrl, sharedConnectionsCount. No company size/industry/activity fields exist in this output (spec §7's company-context factor and the spec's 'LinkedIn activity indicators' output field are both genuinely unavailable from this data source).

nodes.name: Top 4 Per Company
nodes.notes: Groups all scored candidates from this run by Company, sorts each group by Score descending, keeps only the top 4. Runs once with all items (not per-item like the nodes upstream), so it correctly compares candidates against each other within the same company rather than writing every scored candidate regardless of rank.

nodes.name: Mark Company Done
nodes.notes: Matches by Company Name (not ContainerId — that was a run-level ID never actually written to the Companies sheet under the current single-launch-per-run design, so it silently matched nothing). Fires once per top-4 candidate written for that company (up to 4x), idempotently setting Status=Done each time — harmless repetition, not a bug. This is what gives you real per-company completion tracking: filter the Companies sheet on Status to see which companies actually got prospects written vs which are still Pending, independent of whether PhantomBuster itself finished scraping them (check PhantomBuster's own Watcher Mode setting for that side of resumability — it skips companies already scraped in a prior run, so an interrupted multi-company run won't restart from zero).
